sources.name: GDELT DOC 2.0 API (full-text news search, 65 languages, rolling 3 months)
sources.access_method: REST API (JSON / JSONP / CSV / RSS / RSSARCHIVE / JSONFeed / HTML)
endpoints: https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc?query={URLENCODED_QUERY}&mode=ArtList&format=json&maxrecords=250&timespan=24h&sort=DateDesc
https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc?query={Q}&mode=ArtList&format=json&maxrecords=250&startdatetime=20261101000000&enddatetime=20261102000000&sort=DateDesc
https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc?query={Q}&mode=ArtList&format=rss&maxrecords=250&timespan=1h   (RSS output of the same search, usable by feedparser)
https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc?query={Q}&mode=ArtList&format=jsonfeed&timespan=24h   (JSONFeed output, ArtList only per GDELT blog)
https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc?query={Q}&mode=TimelineVol&format=json&timespan=3m   (coverage-volume timeline: a 'news intensity' indicator)
Example honey queries (UNVERIFIED that each operator spelling is accepted; test one first):
query=(honey OR "raw honey") (export OR import OR price OR tariff OR antidumping OR adulteration) sourcelang:english -"Honey Singh" -PayPal
query=miele (prezzo OR prezzi OR import OR export OR apicoltori OR frode) sourcelang:italian -lavatrice -lavastoviglie -elettrodomestici
query=miel (exportación OR precio OR apicultores OR exportaciones) sourcecountry:argentina
query="mật ong" (xuất khẩu OR giá) sourcelang:vietnamese
query=蜂蜜 出口 sourcecountry:china
sources.cost_licensing: Free. GDELT about page (snippet seen): datasets are 'available for unlimited and unrestricted use for any academic, commercial, or governmental use of any kind', redistribution allowed, but 'any use or redistribution of the data must include a citation to the GDELT Project and a link to this website'. Show 'Source: The GDELT Project (gdeltproject.org)' in the UI. GDELT only returns URL, title and metadata. The article text still belongs to each publisher, so the licensing notes in the recommendation apply to anything fetched beyond the title.
sources.update_frequency: Index updates every 15 minutes (from memory, unverified). Searches the rolling last ~3 months only (confirmed by search snippets and the gdeltdoc docs: 'officially only supports the most recent 3 months').
sources.data_available: ArtList mode: per article url, url_mobile, title, seendate, socialimage, domain, language, sourcecountry (column list confirmed by the gdeltdoc PyPI docs and the finance-query Rust crate). No summary or body text. language and sourcecountry come back as English full names (e.g. 'Italian', 'Italy'), from memory, unverified. Timeline modes return volume or tone per time step. Query operators (from memory; the official blog post exists but its text could not be fetched): "exact phrase", (a OR b) where OR must be inside parentheses, -exclude, domain:, domainis:, sourcecountry: (full name without spaces, or FIPS 2-letter code), sourcelang: (name or 3-letter code), theme: (GKG theme), near20:"a b", repeat3:"word", tone<-5, toneabs>5. Params: mode (ArtList, ArtGallery, ImageCollage..., TimelineVol, TimelineVolRaw, TimelineTone, TimelineLang, TimelineSourceCountry, ToneChart), format (html, csv, rss, rssarchive, json, jsonp, jsonfeed), timespan (e.g. 15min, 1h, 24h, 7d, 2w, 3m), startdatetime/enddatetime (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS UTC), maxrecords (max 250; default believed to be 75), sort (DateDesc, DateAsc, ToneDesc, ToneAsc, HybridRel).
sources.parsing_notes: 1) An empty result comes back as '{}' with no 'articles' key. Use data.get('articles', []) (from memory). 2) Query errors are returned as PLAIN TEXT, often with HTTP 200 (e.g. a message about a phrase being too short or a keyword being too common). Check response.headers['content-type'] before calling .json(). 3) The throttle message is plain text, 'Please limit requests to one every 5 seconds' (quoted in finance-query client.rs), possibly with HTTP 429 and no Retry-After header. Sleep 5 s or more between calls and back off on that text. 4) seendate format is 'YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ' (UTC); parse with datetime.strptime(s, '%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ'). It is when GDELT first saw the article, not the publish time. 5) Payloads have occasionally contained invalid control characters. Use json.loads(r.text, strict=False) as a fallback. 6) sourcecountry: filter uses FIPS 10-4 codes, NOT ISO (gdeltdoc docs confirm FIPS). From memory: China=CH, Vietnam=VM, Ukraine=UP, Serbia=RI, Spain=SP, Germany=GM, Argentina=AR, Brazil=BR, India=IN, Italy=IT. Full names avoid the confusion. 7) Very short or very common words can be rejected. Keep phrases specific. 8) Noise to exclude: 'Honey Singh', PayPal 'Honey' extension, Miele appliances (IT/DE/EN), 'luna de miel' (ES), Portuguese 'Mel' as a first name (Mel Gibson, Mel B). 9) Translingual: GDELT machine-translates non-English coverage, and English keywords MAY match translated text (from memory, unverified). Query native-language terms anyway and filter with sourcelang. 10) Dedupe on url, and also on (title, domain) because syndication repeats stories.
sources.rate_limits: No formal quota is documented. GDELT's server message asks for at most one request every 5 seconds (per third-party client source code). Use 6 s spacing and a global lock in the scheduler.

sources.cost_licensing: IMPORTANT RESTRICTION. Feeder's knowledge base (snippet) says each Google News feed is meant 'for use in a personal feed reader for personal, non-commercial use'. From memory, the feed's own <copyright> element reads approximately: 'This XML feed is made available solely for the purpose of rendering Google News results within a personal feed reader for personal, non-commercial use. Any other use of the feed is expressly prohibited.' Feeding a company's market-intelligence tool is arguably commercial use, so Parodi should decide whether to accept that risk. If used, keep it off by default, internal only, low frequency, and store headline + source + link only. There is no official API and no SLA.
sources.data_available: Up to ~100 items per feed (from memory). Per item: title (format 'Headline - Publisher'), link (opaque Google redirect), guid, pubDate (RFC 822, GMT), description (HTML snippet containing only an <a> with the headline and a <font> with the publisher, not a real summary), source (text = publisher name, attribute url = publisher homepage). Query operators: when:1h / when:7d / when:1y, after:YYYY-MM-DD, before:YYYY-MM-DD, site:, intitle:, "exact", OR, -exclude. Spaces become + or %20 and quotes become %22.
sources.parsing_notes: 1) Since 2024 the item <link> (https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMi...?oc=5) is opaque and NOT base64-decodable. Resolving it needs an extra page fetch plus a POST to Google's batchexecute endpoint (the googlenewsdecoder PyPI package does this). That adds ToS and rate-limit risk. Prefer to store the Google link and let the user's browser follow the redirect. 2) Strip the ' - Publisher' suffix from the title using the <source> text (rsplit(' - ', 1)). 3) feedparser exposes the source as entry.source.title and entry.source.href (from memory). 4) Deduplicate across queries on (normalized title, source.href). 5) 'when:' goes inside q, not as a separate param. 6) hl/gl/ceid must agree, or Google redirects or returns another edition. 7) Expect HTTP 429/503 or consent redirects when polling aggressively. Use conditional GET and back off.
sources.rate_limits: Undocumented. Practical guidance: ≤1 request per query per 30-60 min, a few seconds between requests, a realistic User-Agent, and exponential backoff on 429/503.

sources.data_available: Per item (from memory, unverified): title, link (bing.com/news/apiclick.aspx?...&url=<url-encoded original>&...), description (a short publisher snippet, unlike Google News), pubDate, plus News:Source and News:Image in a 'News' namespace. Typically ~10-20 items.
sources.parsing_notes: The original URL can be recovered from the 'url' query parameter of the apiclick link (urllib.parse.parse_qs). The parameter is written as format=rss or format=RSS in different sources; both reportedly work. The namespace URI for News:* is non-standard, so feedparser may expose these as entry['news_source']. Verify against a live sample. The feature can break without notice.
sources.rate_limits: Undocumented; bot detection is likely. If used at all, stay at ≤ a few requests per hour.

sources.data_available: Atom entries: id, title (HTML with <b> highlights), link href (google.com/url?rct=j&sa=t&url=<ORIGINAL URL>&ct=ga&cd=...&usg=...), published, updated, content (a short snippet with <b> tags). Covers news and web.
sources.parsing_notes: Extract the original article from the 'url' query parameter of the link. This is simpler than decoding Google News links. Strip <b> tags from the title and content. The alert set is managed manually in the Google UI, not by the app. Entire field layout is from memory and unverified.

recommendation:
CAVEAT FIRST. During this research every publisher host was blocked from the research sandbox: curl got a 403 from the proxy, and WebFetch got ENOTFOUND for beeculture.com, americanbeejournal.com, informamiele.it, foodsafetynews.com, blog.gdeltproject.org and newscatcherapi.com. The shared WebSearch budget also ran out partway through. Only GDELT, Google News RSS, Bing and the Bee Culture / ABJ / Apimondia site structures are backed by search evidence. Everything else is from memory and is flagged in each entry. A follow-up search pass, or allowing those hosts, would firm them up. Design the collector to self-verify: run feed autodiscovery on first use and automatically deactivate feeds that fail repeatedly.

ORDER OF INTEGRATION
1) GDELT DOC 2.0 first: the backbone. It is the only aggregator whose licence clearly allows commercial use (attribution and a link to gdeltproject.org are required). It returns clean JSON, covers 65 languages, and filters by sourcelang/sourcecountry, which covers Argentina, China, Ukraine, Serbia, Brazil, Vietnam and India without per-country scrapers.
- Use mode=ArtList, format=json, maxrecords=250, sort=DateDesc, and timespan=2h on a 60-min schedule (the overlap absorbs indexing delay). One saved query per language/market, roughly 10-15 queries: EN, IT, ES-AR, PT-BR, ZH, UK, VI, SR, plus EN with sourcecountry:india. Add negative terms for Miele appliances, Honey Singh, PayPal Honey and 'luna de miel'.
- Run all GDELT calls through one global rate limiter with ≥6 s spacing.
- Parse defensively: check the content-type, use data.get('articles', []), and parse seendate with '%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ'.
- Store url, title, seendate, domain, language, sourcecountry.
- Optionally pull mode=TimelineVol weekly per query as a 'news intensity' signal next to price charts.

2) Direct trade-press feeds second, via feedparser with conditional GET (keep etag/modified per feed in SQLite). Start with Bee Culture /feed/, American Bee Journal /feed/, Apimondia /category/news/feed/ and Food Safety News (/tag/honey/feed/, falling back to /?s=honey&feed=rss2). Add Informamiele (Osservatorio Nazionale Miele) after checking by hand; it may be the best Italian price-related source. Use the WordPress conventions entry: try /feed/, then the ?s=…&feed=rss2 search feed, then wp-json. Poll hourly to daily. Apply a keyword relevance filter, and use the Food Safety News sildenafil/'royal honey' exclusion.

3) Crossref API for Bee World and the Journal of Apicultural Research (CC0 metadata, official API; daily). Avoid scraping tandfonline.com.

4) Google News RSS: an optional recall booster, disabled by default. It has the best recall for Italian and Argentine local press and for site: queries (Agrofy, Clarín, FoodNavigator, Latifundist). However, the feed's own notice limits use to a 'personal feed reader for personal, non-commercial use', which a corporate intelligence tool arguably breaches. Expose it as an opt-in setting that Parodi management consciously enables. If enabled, poll each query ≤ hourly with backoff. Do not decode the opaque article links server-side (decoding needs extra Google calls); keep the Google link and the <source url>. Google Alerts RSS is a similar alternative whose links carry the original URL in a url= parameter.

5) Skip Bing News RSS. The official API was retired on 11 Aug 2025, and the format=rss web output is undocumented and covered only by Microsoft's general terms.

6) EU institutional sources: DG AGRI honey page and JRC monthly food-fraud PDFs, monthly via pdfplumber. EU reuse policy is permissive. EC press can also be captured through GDELT domain:europa.eu.

DATA MODEL / PIPELINE
- feeds table: id, name, kind (gdelt | rss | gnews | crossref | pdf), url_or_query, lang, country, poll_minutes, etag, last_modified, last_success, fail_count, active.
- articles table: id, canonical_url (strip utm_*, fbclid, AMP suffixes), url_hash UNIQUE, title, source_name, source_domain, published_utc, lang, country, summary_short (≤300 chars, HTML stripped), tags (countries / varieties / topics), relevance_score, first_seen, feed_id.
- Dedupe: unique on url_hash, then a near-duplicate title check on the same day (rapidfuzz ratio > 90).
- Tagging dictionaries:
  - origins: Argentina, China, Ukraine, Serbia, Brazil, Vietnam, India, Mexico, Turkey, ...
  - varieties: acacia/robinia, orange blossom/zagara/agrumi/azahar, chestnut/castagno, lavender/lavanda, dandelion/tarassaco, sunflower/girasole/girasol, eucalyptus, clover/trifoglio, multifloral/millefiori/polyflora
  - topics: price, export/import, tariff/antidumping/countervailing, adulteration/fraud/NMR, harvest/drought/crop, regulation (Breakfast Directive, 2001/110/EC, origin labelling), EU-Ukraine quota.
- Relevance = (honey term present) AND (market/trade term OR origin country), after the exclusion lists.
- Send a descriptive User-Agent such as 'ParodiHoneyIntel/1.0 (+company contact URL)'. Honour robots.txt for any HTML fetch. Space requests ≥1 min per host for publishers.

LICENSING POLICY (store vs full text)
- Store headline, link, source, date and your own tags, plus at most a short excerpt (≤300 chars, as supplied by the feed). This is the defensible default. Under EU DSM Directive Art. 15 (press publishers' right; implemented in Italy as Art. 43-bis of L. 633/1941), hyperlinks and 'individual words or very short extracts' are excluded, and US practice treats headlines and links as low-risk.
- Do NOT store or redisplay full article text (content:encoded or scraped bodies). Full-content RSS is licensed for reading, not archiving or redistribution, and paywalled sources (ABJ magazine, APK-Inform, UkrAgroConsult, T&F) must never be fetched beyond their public teasers.
- Transient full-text processing for classification can fall under the EU text-and-data-mining exception (DSM Art. 4; Italy Art. 70-quater): it applies to lawfully accessed content unless the rightsholder has opted out in machine-readable form (robots.txt / TDM-reservation). Copies must not be kept longer than needed. Practically: fetch, classify, discard the body, and keep only the metadata.
- Show attribution: 'Source: The GDELT Project' for GDELT results and the publisher name on every item.
- Because the app runs on one desktop for internal use and does not republish, risk stays low as long as it remains internal. Revisit before sharing digests externally, such as emailing customers.
